dependency.description: Downstream dependency (database, broker, HTTP API) by logical name.

domain.description: Business domain that owns the emitting service. Injected centrally from Config.Domain / OBSERVABILITY_DOMAIN.

environment.description: Deployment environment. Injected centrally from Config.Environment, else APP_ENV, else ENVIRONMENT (trimmed, lowercased; no aliases, so production is rejected: use prod). Same precedence in every platform library.

event_type.description: Event envelope type (<domain>.<entity>.<past-tense-verb>[.v<N>]). Bounded by the emitter: unknown when empty, __oversized__ over 128 bytes, __other__ once the process limit of distinct values (platform-events default 200) is reached.
event_type.cardinality: bounded by the event catalogue and the per-process event_type limit

grpc_method.description: Full gRPC method name (/package.Service/Method), or unknown.

label.description: Name of a label whose values were replaced to bound cardinality.

library.description: Platform library reporting its build, by repository name. Go and Python ports are distinct values because they have separate version streams.

library_version.description: Module version of the library the service was built with (e.g. v1.6.0), devel for an unreleased build.

method.description: HTTP request method. Methods outside the standard set are reported as OTHER.

operation.description: Logical operation from the fixed per-metric set declared in the registry entry (e.g. consume, outbox_publish, SQL verbs SELECT/INSERT).

outcome.description: success: completed as intended; failure: rejected for a business reason; error: system or transport fault. Each metric declares the subset it uses.

pool.description: Database pool name from Config.PoolName (e.g. default, primary, replica), static per deployment.

queue.description: Queue name: the last path segment of the queue URL (e.g. orders, orders.fifo), never the full URL; unknown when empty.

reason.description: Failure or routing reason from a fixed per-metric enum, snake_case. Never an error message.

route.description: Gin route template (e.g. /api/items/:id), or unknown for unmatched requests. Never the raw URL path.

service.description: Emitting service (e.g. event-consumer). Injected centrally from Config.ServiceName / the library Identity. Same rule as platform-events and platform-pgcommon identities.

source.description: Origin system of a change or event, snake_case.

status_class.description: Response class. HTTP 1xx-3xx and gRPC OK are 2xx; client-side gRPC codes are 4xx; everything else is 5xx.

strategy.description: Resolution or authentication strategy from a fixed set, snake_case.

topic.description: Topic name: the last segment of the topic ARN (e.g. iam-events, orders.fifo), never the full ARN; unknown when empty.

transport.description: Inbound transport of the request: http or grpc.

version.description: Build version of the emitting binary (Config.BuildVersion / BUILD_VERSION; unknown when unset). Only on build-info metrics: a per-build label on every series would multiply series on each deploy.

violation_type.description: Row-level-security violation class recorded in rls_violation_log by rls_check_tenant() and the service's own checks, snake_case; other for anything outside the set.

metrics.name: platform_build_info
metrics.help: Always 1; the version label carries the build of the emitting service.
metrics.aggregation: count by (domain, environment, version) for rollout tracking; never summed.

metrics.name: platform_http_requests_total
metrics.help: HTTP requests completed by the server, including recovered panics (counted as 5xx).
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment, ...) of rate(); safe to sum across services and domains.

metrics.name: platform_http_request_duration_seconds
metrics.help: HTTP server request latency in seconds, measured by MetricsMiddleware.
metrics.aggregation: histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket); buckets are identical in every service.

metrics.name: platform_http_request_size_bytes
metrics.help: HTTP request body size in bytes from Content-Length (not observed when the length is unknown, e.g. chunked uploads).
metrics.aggregation: histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket).

metrics.name: platform_http_response_size_bytes
metrics.help: HTTP response body size in bytes.
metrics.aggregation: histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket).

metrics.name: platform_http_active_requests
metrics.help: HTTP requests currently being handled.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment); also an HPA signal.

metrics.name: platform_http_panics_total
metrics.help: HTTP handler panics recovered by the middleware stack.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment) of increase().

metrics.name: platform_http_rate_limited_requests_total
metrics.help: HTTP requests answered with 429 Too Many Requests.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment, route) of rate().

metrics.name: platform_http_request_timeouts_total
metrics.help: HTTP requests whose TimeoutMiddleware deadline expired before the handler responded.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment, route) of rate().

metrics.name: platform_grpc_server_handled_total
metrics.help: gRPC server RPCs completed, including recovered panics (counted as Internal).
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment, ...) of rate(); safe to sum across services and domains.

metrics.name: platform_grpc_server_handling_seconds
metrics.help: gRPC server RPC latency in seconds.
metrics.aggregation: histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket); buckets are identical in every service.

metrics.name: platform_grpc_server_request_size_bytes
metrics.help: gRPC request message size in bytes (sum over messages for streams).
metrics.aggregation: histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket).

metrics.name: platform_grpc_server_response_size_bytes
metrics.help: gRPC response message size in bytes (sum over messages for streams).
metrics.aggregation: histogram_quantile over sum by (le, ...) of rate(_bucket).

metrics.name: platform_grpc_server_inflight_requests
metrics.help: gRPC server RPCs currently being handled.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment); also an HPA signal.

metrics.name: platform_grpc_rate_limited_requests_total
metrics.help: gRPC RPCs that ended with ResourceExhausted.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment, grpc_method) of rate().

metrics.name: platform_grpc_panics_total
metrics.help: gRPC handler panics recovered by the interceptor stack.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, environment) of increase().

metrics.name: platform_unclassified_errors_total
metrics.help: Errors that reached the top-level error handler unclassified and were answered as a generic internal error (HTTP 500 internal-error, gRPC Internal): a programming defect.
metrics.aggregation: Alert on any: sum by (domain, service, environment) (increase(platform_unclassified_errors_total[5m])) > 0. Trend: sum by (domain, service, transport) (rate(platform_unclassified_errors_total[1h])).
metrics.governance_notes: Approved 2026-10-16 (platform-gincommon LLD OQ-25). Emitted by platform-gincommon (HTTP error handler, gRPC error sanitizer) and platform-fastapicommon (UnhandledErrorMiddleware, gRPC interceptor). Both transports are initialised to 0 so the first error is visible to increase(). Which route or method failed is in the retained 'unclassified error' log event; it is deliberately not a label.

metrics.name: platform_messages_received_total
metrics.help: A message delivered to a consumer by its queue (one per SQS delivery, redeliveries included), counted on receipt before it is parsed.
metrics.aggregation: Inbound rate per service: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[5m])). Platform-wide: sum by (domain) (…).
metrics.governance_notes: Canonical name per the standard. queue is an approved dimension; its value is the queue name, not the URL.

metrics.name: platform_messages_processed_total
metrics.help: A received message whose handler completed successfully, after which the message was acknowledged (deleted). Messages dead-lettered instead are counted in platform_dlq_messages_total, not here.
metrics.aggregation: Success ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_processed_total[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[5m])).
metrics.cardinality: queue (≤5) × event_type (registered types a service consumes, typically ≤30).
metrics.governance_notes: Canonical name per the standard. event_type is an approved dimension.

metrics.name: platform_messages_failed_total
metrics.help: A received message that could not be processed on this delivery, by reason: malformed (not a valid envelope), decode_error (schema-registry codec failure), handler_error, handler_panic, or dead_letter_error (dead-letter handling or DLQ forwarding failed). A failed message is retried or dead-lettered; see platform_retry_total and platform_dlq_messages_total.
metrics.aggregation: Failure ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_failed_total[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[5m])). Poison producers: sum by (domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_messages_failed_total{reason="malformed"}[15m])).
metrics.cardinality: queue (≤5) × event_type (≤30) × reason (5); malformed always has event_type=unknown.
metrics.governance_notes: Canonical name per the standard. The reason vocabulary is requested for approval. Values emitted by platform-events: reason ∈ {malformed, decode_error, handler_error, handler_panic, dead_letter_error}. Other emitters use the global label vocabulary; governance to decide whether to ratify a closed platform-wide enum.

metrics.name: platform_retry_total
metrics.help: An attempt that failed and was left for automatic retry: a consumed message whose processing failed and stays on its queue for redelivery (operation=consume), or an outbox publish that failed with attempts remaining (operation=outbox_publish).
metrics.aggregation: Retry pressure per service: sum by (domain, service, operation) (rate(platform_retry_total[5m])).
metrics.governance_notes: Canonical name per the standard, but IAM services already register platform_retry_total with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint}; {event_type,reason}). In such a service registration is refused and reported as a RegistrationWarning (fail-soft), so the reference alerts do not depend on this metric until governance approves ONE label vocabulary. Values emitted by platform-events: operation ∈ {consume, outbox_publish}. Other emitters use the global label vocabulary; governance to decide whether to ratify a closed platform-wide enum.

metrics.name: platform_dlq_messages_total
metrics.help: A message moved to dead-letter storage: forwarded to its SQS queue's RedrivePolicy DLQ (operation=consume), or moved to outbox_dead_letters after exhausting its publish attempts (operation=outbox_publish), by reason.
metrics.aggregation: Dead-letter inflow: sum by (domain, service, operation, reason) (increase(platform_dlq_messages_total[15m])). Any sustained non-zero rate needs attention.
metrics.governance_notes: Canonical name per the standard. operation and reason vocabularies are requested for approval. Values emitted by platform-events: operation ∈ {consume, outbox_publish}; reason ∈ {malformed, decode_error, max_receive_count, explicit, max_attempts}. Other emitters use the global label vocabulary; governance to decide whether to ratify a closed platform-wide enum.

metrics.name: platform_duplicate_messages_total
metrics.help: A redelivered message acknowledged without running its handler because the consumer's dedup ledger (inbox processed_events) had already recorded its event ID.
metrics.aggregation: Duplicate ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_duplicate_messages_total[15m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_messages_received_total[15m])).
metrics.governance_notes: Registry-proposed example in the standard. The legacy metric's consumer label is replaced by queue.

metrics.name: platform_dependency_request_seconds
metrics.help: Client-observed wall time of one call to an external dependency — SNS (publish, publish_batch), SQS (receive_message, delete_message, change_message_visibility, send_message, get_queue_attributes, get_queue_url) or the configured schema-registry codec (encode, decode) — by outcome. The _count series counts calls. receive_message is a long poll: its duration includes up to WaitTimeSeconds (default 20 s) of waiting on an empty queue, so exclude it from latency views (it stays meaningful for error rates).
metrics.aggregation: Error ratio: sum by (domain, service, dependency) (rate(platform_dependency_request_seconds_count{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, dependency) (rate(platform_dependency_request_seconds_count[5m])). p99 (long-poll receives excluded): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service, dependency, operation) (rate(platform_dependency_request_seconds_bucket{operation!="receive_message"}[5m]))).
metrics.cardinality: dependency × operation (10 valid pairs) × outcome (2) × 12 buckets.
metrics.governance_notes: Registry-proposed example in the standard. IAM services register this name with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}); platform-events uses {dependency,operation,outcome}. Where a service's registry already holds another shape the metric is disabled with a RegistrationWarning (fail-soft). Values emitted by platform-events: dependency ∈ {sns, sqs, codec}; operation ∈ {publish, publish_batch, receive_message, delete_message, change_message_visibility, send_message, get_queue_attributes, get_queue_url, encode, decode}; outcome ∈ {success, error}. Other emitters use the global label vocabulary; governance to decide whether to ratify a closed platform-wide enum.

metrics.name: platform_event_propagation_seconds
metrics.help: Time from an event's creation (envelope `time`, set by the producer) to its FIRST receipt by a consumer (ApproximateReceiveCount ≤ 1) — end-to-end propagation delay through the outbox, SNS and SQS. Redeliveries are not observed, so retry delay does not inflate it. Negative clock skew is clamped to 0.
metrics.aggregation: p95 propagation per consumer: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_event_propagation_seconds_bucket[5m]))). Includes producer clock skew.
metrics.governance_notes: Registry-proposed example in the standard. New signal (no legacy predecessor).

metrics.name: platform_queue_depth
metrics.help: Messages waiting on a consumer's queue to be received (SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages — visible, not in flight or delayed), sampled by the consumer every WithQueueDepthMetrics interval. Approximate by SQS design.
metrics.aggregation: Every replica samples the same queue, so aggregate with max, not sum: max by (domain, service, queue) (platform_queue_depth). The natural HPA/KEDA scaling signal once ratified.
metrics.governance_notes: Registry-proposed example in the standard. Emitted by platform-events because consuming services may not use the SQS SDK themselves (depguard); opt-in (WithQueueDepthMetrics) since each replica polls sqs:GetQueueAttributes.

metrics.name: platform_dlq_depth
metrics.help: Messages sitting in the dead-letter queue attached to a consumer's queue by its RedrivePolicy (SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages of the DLQ), sampled with platform_queue_depth. queue is the SOURCE queue's name, so the gauge joins with the consumer's other queue metrics.
metrics.aggregation: max by (domain, service, queue) (platform_dlq_depth) > 0 — messages awaiting investigation or replay. Complements platform_dlq_messages_total (inflow) with the backlog.
metrics.governance_notes: Registry-proposed example in the standard. Not emitted when the queue has no RedrivePolicy.

metrics.name: platform_messages_in_flight
metrics.help: Messages a consumer has received and is currently processing (decode, dead-letter routing or handler), per replica. At the consumer's concurrency limit for long periods means the replica is saturated; a value that never drops points at a hung handler (see WithHandlerTimeout).
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, queue) (platform_messages_in_flight) for total work in progress; compare per replica against the configured concurrency for saturation.
metrics.governance_notes: Proposed by platform-events. Complements platform_queue_depth (waiting) with work in progress.

metrics.name: platform_messages_published_total
metrics.help: One event a producer attempted to publish to a topic, by outcome (error includes validation, encoding and broker failures; a batch counts each message).
metrics.aggregation: Publish error ratio: sum by (domain, service, topic) (rate(platform_messages_published_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, topic) (rate(platform_messages_published_total[5m])).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified. The producer-side counterpart of platform_messages_received_total; requests approval of a topic label.

metrics.name: platform_message_processing_duration_seconds
metrics.help: Wall time a consumer's handler (or dead-letter handler) spent on one delivery, whatever the outcome.
metrics.aggregation: p99 handler latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_message_processing_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified.

metrics.name: platform_outbox_pending_events
metrics.help: Events in a service's transactional outbox that are due to be published (unpublished, not leased and not waiting out a retry backoff), sampled every outbox GaugeInterval (default 15s) and capped at 100000 (a reading of 100000 means at least that many). Left at its last value when the count query fails (see platform_outbox_errors_total{operation="pending_count"}).
metrics.aggregation: Backlog per service: max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_pending_events) — every runner reads the same table, so use max, not sum.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified.

metrics.name: platform_outbox_leased_events
metrics.help: Unpublished outbox events not yet due: claimed by a runner and being published, or waiting out a retry backoff. Sampled every GaugeInterval, capped at 100000.
metrics.aggregation: max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_leased_events).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified.

metrics.name: platform_outbox_oldest_pending_age
metrics.help: Age of the oldest unpublished outbox event (now − created_at), 0 when nothing is unpublished, sampled every GaugeInterval. Transient publish failures never dead-letter, so this is the signal that delivery has stopped even when the backlog is small (e.g. a credential outage on a low-volume service).
metrics.aggregation: max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_oldest_pending_age) — every runner reads the same table. Alert on it staying above the delivery-latency objective (e.g. > 600 for 10m) once ratified.
metrics.governance_notes: Proposed by platform-events. Left at its last value when the query fails (platform_outbox_errors_total{operation="oldest_pending"}).

metrics.name: platform_outbox_ordering_blocked_events
metrics.help: Ordered outbox events (outbox.EnqueueOrdered) waiting behind an earlier unpublished record with the same ordering key. Sampled every GaugeInterval, capped at 100000. A value that keeps growing means a key's head record keeps failing and holds the rest of its key.
metrics.aggregation: max by (domain, service) (platform_outbox_ordering_blocked_events) — every runner reads the same table.
metrics.governance_notes: Proposed by platform-events with per-key ordering. Left at its last value when the query fails (platform_outbox_errors_total{operation="blocked_count"}).

metrics.name: platform_message_timeouts_total
metrics.help: A received message whose WithHandlerTimeout deadline expired, by the stage it expired in: decode (codec decode), dead_letter_handler, or handler. Each is also counted in platform_messages_failed_total under its usual reason (decode_error, dead_letter_error, handler_error) — this counter separates timeouts from other failures without changing that Canonical metric's vocabulary.
metrics.aggregation: Timeout share of failures: sum by (domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_message_timeouts_total[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, queue) (rate(platform_messages_failed_total[5m])).
metrics.governance_notes: Proposed by platform-events. Emitted only when the consumer uses WithHandlerTimeout.

metrics.name: platform_outbox_publish_attempts_total
metrics.help: One attempt by the outbox runner to publish a claimed outbox event, by outcome.
metrics.aggregation: Outbox publish error ratio: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_outbox_publish_attempts_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_outbox_publish_attempts_total[5m])).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified.

metrics.name: platform_outbox_errors_total
metrics.help: An outbox runner step that failed outside a publish attempt: poll (claiming a batch), unmarshal (a stored envelope that no longer parses), mark_published (an event published but not marked — it will be delivered again), pending_count / leased_count / oldest_pending / blocked_count (a gauge query).
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, operation) (rate(platform_outbox_errors_total[5m])) > 0.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified.

metrics.name: platform_outbox_dead_letter_operations_total
metrics.help: Outbox dead-letter records acted on by an operator call: reprocess (moved back to outbox_events for retry) or discard (permanently deleted). Counts records, not calls.
metrics.aggregation: Audit trail: sum by (domain, service, operation) (increase(platform_outbox_dead_letter_operations_total[1d])).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified.

metrics.name: platform_telemetry_label_overflow_total
metrics.help: A label value the library replaced because it exceeded its cardinality bound: event_type over 128 bytes → `__oversized__`, or a new distinct event_type beyond the per-process limit (default 200) → `__other__`. Counts replacements. Non-zero means a misconfigured or adversarial producer, or a limit set below the service's real number of event types.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (domain, service, label) (rate(platform_telemetry_label_overflow_total[15m])) > 0.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified.

metrics.name: platform_library_info
metrics.help: Always 1. Identifies a platform library and the version a service was built with, for fleet-wide upgrade tracking.
metrics.aggregation: Services still on an old version: count by (library_version) (platform_library_info{library="platform-events"}).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Shadow-emitted until ratified. Intended to be shared by every platform library (platform-pgcommon, platform-gincommon); the legacy build_info carried the service's own version, which is not in the Tier 1 vocabulary. Every platform library reports itself here, so library uses the global vocabulary (platform-events emits library="platform-events").

metrics.name: platform_db_queries_total
metrics.help: One statement a service executed against PostgreSQL through a pgcommon pool — a query, a SendBatch (operation=BATCH) or a CopyFrom (operation=COPY) — counted when it completes, by outcome. Statements pgcommon issues itself (RLS GUC set_config on acquire, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints, the PgBouncer wrapping transaction) are excluded unless they fail: a failed COMMIT or GUC injection is a failure of the caller's work.
metrics.aggregation: Error ratio per service: sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_db_queries_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service) (rate(platform_db_queries_total[5m])). Platform-wide database load: sum by (domain) (rate(platform_db_queries_total[5m])).
metrics.cardinality: pool (≤3) × operation (closed allowlist, only observed verbs materialise) × outcome (2). SQL text is never a label.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_query_duration_seconds
metrics.help: Client-observed wall time of one statement (query, SendBatch or CopyFrom) against PostgreSQL through a pgcommon pool, from send to result. Library-internal statements (RLS GUC set_config, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints) are excluded unless they fail: a failed COMMIT or GUC injection is a failure of the caller's work.
metrics.aggregation: p99 per service: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service) (rate(platform_db_query_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))). Buckets are identical in every service, so cross-service quantiles are valid.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_pool_acquires_total
metrics.help: One attempt to check a connection out of a pgcommon pool (WithConn, RunInTx and helpers), by outcome; error includes acquire timeouts (context deadline exceeded while waiting) and a closed pool. An attempt abandoned by the caller (context cancelled) is not counted under either outcome; its wait is still recorded in platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds.
metrics.aggregation: Acquire failure ratio: sum by (domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_acquires_total{outcome="error"}[5m])) / sum by (domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_acquires_total[5m])).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds
metrics.help: Time a caller waited to check a connection out of a pgcommon pool, recorded for every attempt including failures — a saturation signal.
metrics.aggregation: p99 wait per pool: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_slow_queries_total
metrics.help: A statement whose wall time exceeded the pool's configured slow-query threshold (Config.SlowQueryThreshold). Counted for every occurrence, independent of log rate limiting. Library-internal statements (RLS GUC set_config, BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, transaction timeouts, savepoints) are excluded.
metrics.aggregation: Thresholds are per-service configuration, so compare trends within a service rather than absolute rates across services.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_transaction_retries_total
metrics.help: A transaction attempt that failed with a retryable PostgreSQL error and was retried by RunInTxWithRetry*: deadlock (SQLSTATE 40P01) or serialization failure (40001).
metrics.aggregation: Contention board: sum by (domain, service, reason) (rate(platform_db_transaction_retries_total[5m])).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_transaction_retries_exhausted_total
metrics.help: A RunInTxWithRetry* call that used every attempt and still failed with a retryable error — the operation failed for the caller.
metrics.aggregation: Any sustained non-zero rate is user-visible failure: sum by (domain, service) (increase(platform_db_transaction_retries_exhausted_total[15m])) > 0.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_pool_connections
metrics.help: Connections currently held by a pgcommon pool, by state: idle (available), acquired (checked out), constructing (being dialled). Sampled at scrape time from the pool's statistics.
metrics.aggregation: Utilisation: sum by (domain, service, pool) (platform_db_pool_connections{state="acquired"}) / sum by (domain, service, pool) (platform_db_pool_max_connections). Total = sum over state.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_pool_max_connections
metrics.help: The configured connection limit of a pgcommon pool (Config.MaxConns).
metrics.aggregation: Denominator for utilisation (see platform_db_pool_connections).
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: platform_db_pool_empty_acquires_total
metrics.help: Cumulative acquires that had to wait because every connection was checked out (pool exhausted). A rising rate means the pool is undersized for the service's concurrency.
metrics.aggregation: Saturation: sum by (domain, service, pool) (rate(platform_db_pool_empty_acquires_total[5m])) > 0.
metrics.governance_notes: New platform_* name (not among the standard's canonical or registry-proposed examples); submitted under the Registry Ratification Requirement. Reviewers should also decide whether the pool/query dimensions belong under a generic shared metric instead — platform_dependency_request_seconds{dependency="postgres"} / platform_retry_total — once those names have ONE approved label vocabulary: today IAM services register them with conflicting label sets ({target_service,endpoint} vs {dependency,operation,outcome}; {event_type,reason}), so pgcommon cannot join them without breaking registration in those services.

metrics.name: iam_auth_events_total
metrics.help: Authentication events (login, logout, token refresh, MFA challenge) observed by an IAM service.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (environment, event_type, outcome) of rate(); identical meaning in every IAM service.

metrics.name: iam_tenant_resolution_total
metrics.help: Attempts to resolve the tenant of a request or event.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (environment, strategy, outcome) of rate().

metrics.name: iam_identity_sync_total
metrics.help: Identity records synchronised from an external identity source.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (environment, source, outcome) of rate().

metrics.name: iam_realm_operations_total
metrics.help: Administrative realm operations (create, update, delete, configure).
metrics.aggregation: sum by (environment, operation, outcome) of rate().

metrics.name: iam_rls_violations_total
metrics.help: Row-level-security violations recorded in the service's rls_violation_log, by violation_type. Fed from a periodic scrape of the log table, not from the request path.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (environment, service, violation_type) of increase(); any increase is a security signal, so alert on > 0 rather than on a ratio.
metrics.governance_notes: Emitted today by iam-org-membership, iam-audit-log and iam-user-profile with the same name and label set (iam-user-profile LLD §11.2 established it). missing_primary_email is written only by iam-user-profile; iam-audit-log maps unknown values to other, the other two pass the stored value through, so the set is bounded by the services' own SQL. Needs an IAM owner before ratification.

metrics.name: iam_auth_session_revoke_failed_total
metrics.help: Calls to the realm provisioner's RevokeUserSessions that errored or returned non-2xx. The caller fails open (AUTH-8), so every increment is a user session that may outlive its membership.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (environment, service, reason) of rate(); alert on sustained rate > 0.
metrics.governance_notes: Emitted today only by iam-org-membership; registered as domain-shared because any IAM service that revokes sessions must report through the same name. iam-org-membership currently emits the raw HTTP status code (e.g. "503") as reason, which the reason vocabulary rejects: it must map codes to http_4xx / http_5xx / http_other before metricslint check passes.

metrics.name: iam_lifecycle_event_skipped_total
metrics.help: Tenant lifecycle events skipped by the recency guard (EVT-14: event time <= the tenant's last applied event time), by event_type.
metrics.aggregation: sum by (environment, service, event_type) of rate(); a sustained rate means out-of-order delivery or a replay.
metrics.governance_notes: Emitted today only by iam-org-membership.

metrics.name: iam_lifecycle_event_lag_seconds
metrics.help: Seconds from a tenant lifecycle event's envelope time to the moment the consumer applied it, by event_type. Sustained high p99 flags a consumer backlog (SLO-3).
metrics.aggregation: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, environment, service, event_type) (rate(iam_lifecycle_event_lag_seconds_bucket[5m]))). Includes producer clock skew.
metrics.governance_notes: Emitted today only by iam-org-membership; the lifecycle_event_lag preset is that service's existing bucket set. Overlaps platform_event_propagation_seconds (envelope time to first receipt) but measures to apply time and includes retries; governance to decide whether to keep both or move to the platform metric and its event_propagation preset.
